name: When Companies Ruled the World
description: Merchant companies with charters, armies, flags and colonies: the East India Companies, Hudson's Bay, the Mississippi and South Sea schemes and the other firms that did the work of states.

checkpoints.name: Charters and shareholders
checkpoints.note: Kings granted merchants charters and monopolies. The English East India Company of 1600 and the Dutch East India Company of 1602 raised money from many investors; the Virginia Company planted the colony of Virginia, Henry Hudson explored for the Dutch, and the Dutch company founded the Cape Colony in 1652.

checkpoints.name: Furs, slaves and bubbles
checkpoints.note: The Royal African Company shipped enslaved Africans in the Atlantic slave trade, and the Hudson's Bay Company was given the fur trade of a vast northern land in 1670. The Mississippi Company in France and the South Sea Company in Britain promised riches and crashed in 1720, while the Swedish East India Company shipped tea from Canton.

checkpoints.name: Company rule
checkpoints.note: Victory at Plassey in 1757 began the East India Company's rule over Bengal and then most of India. The bankrupt Dutch company was wound up in 1799 and its islands became the Dutch East Indies. Company opium sold in China led to the First Opium War, and after the Indian Rebellion of 1857 the Crown took over and the company was dissolved in 1874.

checkpoints.name: The last company states
checkpoints.note: Cecil Rhodes won a royal charter in 1889 for a company that seized the lands later named after him, and the United Fruit Company controlled railways, ports and politics across Central America, helping to topple Guatemala's government in 1954, until it was absorbed in 1970.
